title: Quasi-separated morphism of schemes
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_YX$ be its diagonal, the morphism into the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] whose two components are the identity of $X$. The morphism $f$ is *quasi-separated* if $\Delta_f$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], that is, the inverse image under $\Delta_f$ of every quasi-compact open (equivalently, of every affine open) of $X\times_YX$ is quasi-compact. A scheme $X$ is *quasi-separated* if $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-separated.
